STEP 1 - Scene: A plated lunch/dinner: saffron-style yellow rice, a piece of pan-cooked chicken or fish with herbs, sautéed spinach, and broccoli florets (Romanesco-type).

STEP 2 - Vessel: A large square-ish white dinner plate, roughly 26 cm across. Area ≈ 3.14 x 13^2 ≈ 530 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: (1) yellow rice, (2) cooked chicken/fish pieces, (3) wilted spinach/leafy greens, (4) Romanesco/broccoli florets.

STEP 4 - Area (percent of plate):
- Yellow rice: ~17% (about 90 cm^2)
- Chicken/fish pieces: ~16% (about 85 cm^2)
- Spinach: ~18% (about 95 cm^2)
- Romanesco/broccoli: ~10% (about 53 cm^2)
Total covered ≈ 61%, consistent with the visible plate.

STEP 5 - Volume (area x height):
- Rice: 90 cm^2 x 1.5 cm ≈ 135 ml
- Chicken: 85 cm^2 x 1.2 cm ≈ 102 ml
- Spinach: 95 cm^2 x 1.5 cm ≈ 143 ml
- Romanesco: 53 cm^2 x 2 cm ≈ 106 ml

STEP 6 - Grams (bulk density):
- Rice 135 ml x 0.8 ≈ 108 g
- Chicken 102 ml x 0.95 ≈ 97 g
- Spinach 143 ml x 0.15 ≈ 21 g
- Romanesco 106 ml x 0.6 ≈ 64 g

STEP 7 - Energy (cooked, as plated):
- Rice (saffron/cooked with some oil): ~150 kcal/100 g → 162 kcal
- Chicken/fish: ~190 kcal/100 g (pan-cooked with some fat) → 184 kcal
- Spinach (cooked, oiled): ~30 kcal/100 g → 6 kcal
- Romanesco/broccoli (cooked): ~35 kcal/100 g → 22 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Total ≈ 290 g and ≈ 374 kcal. This is plausible for a plate about 60% covered with a modest portion of each item; no oil sheen is clearly visible, so no extra fat is added.
